contracts.description:
Warwickshire County Council (the Council) is seeking a single provider to deliver an Integrated Public Health Nursing Service in Warwickshire.  This procurement will lead to one contract: 

A Public Health Nursing Service (0-19 years up to 25 with SEND), governed by WCC terms and conditions.   

The scope of the public health nursing service includes the development of a whole family approach to supporting infants, children, and young people in Warwickshire, ensuring they obtain the very best start in life.  Recognising the dynamic system within which these services operate, there is an increased emphasis on joint, collaborative and partnership working with the wider 0-19 (up to 25 with SEND) service partners across the health and social care system.  Collaboration with our voluntary, health and social colleagues can unlock great potential in accelerating improvements in child health and the provider will be expected to embed such principles throughout the service offer. 

The service will provide leadership, coordination and delivery of the Healthy Child Programme as described in national documentation, using an evidence-based approach to deliver against the twelve High Impact Areas along with undertaking all mandated elements (five health and wellbeing development reviews for 0-5's and the NCMP for 5-19s) and developing the health needs assessments at key transition points. 

The service will use a place-based and community centred approach to develop solutions that draw on all assets and resources of an area, integrating and building resilience so that people can take control of their health and wellbeing and influence on factors that underpin good health.

contracts.description:
The aim of this procurement exercise is to appoint an experienced Registered Provider (RP) of Social Housing, that will lead on the development of a purpose-built core and cluster scheme consisting of 6 bungalows to accommodate people with LD/autism with complex needs. 
      
      The new scheme will offer an opportunity for its residents to benefit from an individual bungalow with self-contained private garden, designed to reflect the needs of the individuals who will take on the tenancies, and built to a high standard in line with relevant national design guidelines. 
      The Council has identified a vacant site within its own asset portfolio.  The site is of an appropriate size and location for the proposed development. The proposal includes a disposal of land (on a 125-year lease only) owned by the Council for the above development, and as such, Heads of Terms and subsequent development agreement and lease will underpin these arrangements. 
      It is expected that the appointed RP will be engaged in the procurement activity of the care provider recognising the required close working relationship that is necessary to provide effective accommodation and care for residents.  
      
      The Council, in partnership with Coventry City Council, Coventry and Warwickshire Integrated Care Board (ICB), Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership Trust and NHS England local specialist team, are working to deliver the Transforming Care programme (TCP) within the subregion. The aim of the Programme is to prevent avoidable admissions to specialist Learning Disability (LD) or Mental Health hospitals by autistic people or people with LD and ensure that individuals are discharged back into the community with the appropriate accommodation, help and support.  
      The Learning Disabilities and Autism (LDA) programme has NHS Long Term Plan targets to reduce the number of people with a learning disability and/or autism who are in a specialist LD or mental health hospital

Lot 1 - Youth Service and Third Sector support and development services in Warwickshire

WCC is looking for a Provider (or group of Providers through a Lead Provider) to deliver this Service through a single contract. If the Service is delivered by more than one Provider, the Providers will work together to minimise duplication and ensure a cost effective delivery model.

The Service will deliver within Warwickshire a range of functions that increase the prominence and skills base of the Third Sector and increase levels of volunteering in the delivery of traditionally Public Sector services. The Service will empower the Third Sector to thrive by modelling and encouraging new ways of working and innovative practices, as well as building on existing skills. The Service will help move the Third Sector towards greater sustainability, and support the building of capacity within communities to become more resilient. The Service will work collaboratively to develop an approach to measuring and increasing the impact and social value of the Third Sector. The Service will support the Third Sector to influence Public Sector policy making and
the shaping of local service delivery.

Lot 2 - Advice Services within Warwickshire

WCC is looking for a Provider (or group of Providers through a Lead Provider) to deliver this Service through
a single contract. If the Service is delivered by more than one Provider, the Providers will work together to minimise duplication and ensure a cost effective delivery model.

contracts.title: Reprocessing of plasterboard and gypsum materials from Household Waste Recycling Centres in Warwickshire
contracts.description:
The Authority is tendering for the reprocessing of plasterboard and gypsum materials from Household Waste Recycling Centres (HWRCs) in Warwickshire. The provision of containers (currently 40 yard open skips) and haulage to the contractor’s processing facility or transfer point will be undertaken by the Authority or its appointed haulage contractor, Biffa.

The proposed Contract start date is: 01/11/2015.

The proposed Contract end date is: 31/10/2017.
 
The initial contract term will be 2 years, however the Authority reserves the right to extend the Contract by further periods not exceeding 12 months (12 months being the maximum available extension period) at the discretion of the Authority based on the contract performance of the successful applicant.

This Contract will be reviewed in January 2017.

The estimated total value of the Contract is £90,000.

CSW-Jets will not be used in this instance, due to preference by bidders in this market for paper tenders. All correspondence relating to the project (except for the submission itself) should be sent to: wastetenders@warwickshire.gov.uk.

Submissions should be sent to: Tamalyn Goodwin, Communities, Waste Management Group, Warwickshire County Council, Shire Hall, Market Place, Warwickshire County Council, CV34 4RL.

The deadline for receipt of tenders is 07/08/2015 at 12 (noon).

The deadline for clarifications is 27/07/2015 at 12 (noon).
